findings.evidence: No evals/ directory: no evals/evals.json and no evals/trigger-queries.json.
findings.fix: Add evals/evals.json with at least three realistic prompts (casual, precise, one edge such as a broken mermaid fence or an SVG request under pandoc-latex), expected outputs, input files under evals/files/, and verifiable assertions; add evals/trigger-queries.json with about 20 queries, 8-10 should-trigger and 8-10 should-not-trigger including near-misses (edit a PDF, draw mermaid only, convert to docx).

findings.evidence: Turn a Markdown document with embedded mermaid diagrams into a PDF (or a marp deck) in one non-destructive command: every ```mermaid block is rendered to an image with mmdc, substituted into a temp copy, and that copy is fed to the best complete PDF pipeline installed.
findings.fix: Delete the opening restatement of the description; start at the decision questions.

findings.evidence: Before you run, decide is three binary questions, then a command and a situation table; the thinking does not cover the contradictory ranking or an unknown --backend name.
findings.fix: Add one decision principle: when draft and final disagree with the script's quality order, trust the printed backend and do not re-rank; an unknown --backend name is a script error, not a reason to pick a tool yourself.

findings.evidence: examples/sample-with-mermaid.md is never referenced from SKILL.md or references/backends.md.
findings.fix: Point the primary-flow example at examples/sample-with-mermaid.md when the user has no source file, or drop the file from the skill directory.

findings.evidence: Final → let the quality-ranked auto-selection pick (LaTeX > Typst > WeasyPrint > Chromium).
findings.fix: Replace that parenthetical with the script's actual order from detect_backends.py: pandoc-latex (4) > typst (3) > weasyprint (2) > chromium (1), and say the printed result line is the authority.

findings.evidence: Typst + Pandoc is scored Total 18 and called Winner, while the selection rule two sections later ranks Pandoc+LaTeX first.
findings.fix: State one default: installed pipelines follow quality order Pandoc+LaTeX > Typst > WeasyPrint > Chromium; Typst+Pandoc is only the install recommendation when none is present.

findings.evidence: Exit code 3 (no backend) | Show the printed install command as-is
findings.fix: Say the install text is on stderr and name the three exits: 0 prints Wrote ... (backend, diagrams) on stdout; 2 aborts on stderr with the mermaid line and emits nothing; 3 prints No backend available and, when present, Recommended: install <name>.

findings.evidence: chosen = next(b for b in detect_backends.BACKENDS if b.name == backend_name)
findings.fix: Catch StopIteration and exit with the valid names (pandoc-latex, typst, weasyprint, chromium); argparse already rejects these on the CLI, so this is the programmatic path.

findings.evidence: The Never list covers install, source edits, SVG+LaTeX, single-tool detection, install nagging, and filesystem probes, but not the ranking contradiction an agent will hit.
findings.fix: Add: NEVER re-rank backends from the scored table; Typst's 18/20 is the install-when-absent recommendation, and an already-installed pandoc-latex pipeline outranks it.
